Running the Test Suite

Source: vignettes/running-tests.Rmd
running-tests.Rmd

The testing API works on a pleio object created by run_pleiosim() or by an object with compatible summary-statistic slots.

Shared Inputs

run_pleiotest() calls the internal .pleio_inputs() helper once. It extracts per-phenotype beta, se, and p_value, forms

Zvk=β̂vksêvk, Z_{vk} = \frac{\hat\beta_{vk}}{\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{vk}},

sets non-finite Z-scores to zero, estimates the trait correlation matrix as cor(Z), and computes its eigendecomposition. The MPAT/MTAR methods reuse those shared inputs through the C++ TestEngine.

Full Workflow 

library(pleioverse)
set.seed(21)
pleio <- run_pleiosim(
  n_phenotype = 3,
  n_participant = 1000,
  n_variant_pleiotropic = 5,
  n_variant_nonpleiotropic = c(5, 5, 5),
  n_variant_null = 100,
  heritability = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
)
pleio <- run_pleiotest(pleio, mpat = TRUE, pleiotropy = TRUE, i = 1, j = 2)
head(pleio@results)

Running One Method at a Time

Every individual method returns the modified pleio object, so calls can be chained.

pleio <- run_wald(pleio)
pleio <- run_vc(pleio)
pleio <- run_placo(pleio, i = 1, j = 2)
colnames(pleio@results)

Families in run_pleiotest()

  • mpat = TRUE runs the 24 MPAT/MTAR methods plus tates and metacca.
  • pleiotropy = TRUE runs placo, pgctest, maiup, conjfdr, and polarmorphism.
  • run_acat() is not part of run_pleiotest() because it combines columns that already exist in pleio@results.

Pairwise Pleiotropy Tests

run_placo(), run_pgctest(), run_maiup(), and run_conjfdr() use phenotype indices i and j. A single result column refers only to the pair used in that call.

pair12 <- run_placo(pleio, i = 1, j = 2)
pair13 <- run_placo(pleio, i = 1, j = 3)
